+## Configure Azure RBAC permissions for the server app
+
+The CMG uses the **server/web application's service principal** to deploy and manage its Azure resources. These Azure role-based access control (RBAC) permissions are separate from the Microsoft Entra directory roles used to create app registrations. Assign permissions to the server application's service principal, not the native/client application or the user who runs the console.
+
+Starting in version 2609, shared-key access is automatically disabled for CMG storage. Existing CMGs that previously used shared-key access also need the permissions for Microsoft Entra-authenticated storage and storage role assignments. A successful deployment or update on an earlier version doesn't confirm that these permissions are present.
+
+Verify the following effective permissions at each CMG resource group:
+
+- **Resource management:** Retain the **Contributor** role or equivalent approved permissions that allow the server application to manage the CMG resources.
+- **Storage role assignments:** Allow the server application to manage assignments of the **Storage Blob Data Contributor** and **Storage Table Data Contributor** roles. Contributor alone doesn't grant `Microsoft.Authorization/roleAssignments/write`.
+
+To provide the storage role-assignment permissions with limited delegation:
+
+1. In the Azure portal, open the CMG's resource group and select **Access control (IAM)**.
+2. Identify the service principal for the CMG server application. Verify its application (client) ID and service-principal object ID against the application used by Configuration Manager.
+3. Review its existing role assignments, including inherited assignments and their conditions. If equivalent effective permissions already exist, don't add a duplicate grant.
+4. If the required storage role-assignment permissions are missing, assign **Role Based Access Control Administrator** to this service principal at the CMG resource group. Add a role-assignment condition that allows both `Microsoft.Authorization/roleAssignments/write` and `Microsoft.Authorization/roleAssignments/delete` only for these role definitions:
+
+    - **Storage Blob Data Contributor**: `ba92f5b4-2d11-453d-a403-e96b0029c9fe`
+    - **Storage Table Data Contributor**: `0a9a7e1f-b9d0-4cc4-a60d-0319b160aaa3`
+
+    For instructions to select the allowed roles when configuring the condition, see [Delegate Azure role assignment management to others with conditions](/en-us/azure/role-based-access-control/delegate-role-assignments-portal). Don't use an unrestricted Owner or administrator grant as a shortcut.
+5. Allow time for changes to propagate, then verify that the server application has the required effective permissions. If a custom condition or deny assignment prevents access, have the Azure resource administrator review it rather than broadening permissions or removing the restriction.
+
+The administrator making the assignment needs Azure RBAC permission to create this constrained administrator assignment at the target scope. Permission to create only storage data-role assignments doesn't necessarily authorize the administrator to delegate the **Role Based Access Control Administrator** role. These operator permissions are separate from the permissions granted to the CMG server application.
+
+Important
+
+A grant at a staging resource group doesn't automatically grant access to a different production resource group or a different service principal. Verify each CMG application and resource group, including any inherited permissions and conditions. Being in the same Microsoft Entra tenant isn't sufficient.
+
+If a CMG deployment update fails with HTTP **403**, `DeploymentFailed`, and a denied `Microsoft.Authorization/roleAssignments/write` action in **CloudMgr.log**, review the application object ID and Azure scope in the error. Verify that the indicated service principal can create the required role assignments at that scope. The signed-in administrator having access doesn't establish that the CMG application has access. Also review the failed deployment operations in the Azure portal.
+

 The CMG service requires that you register specific resource providers in your Azure subscription. When you deploy the CMG to a virtual machine scale set, register the following resource providers:

englishSummary.headline: CMG version 2609 adds Azure RBAC requirements
englishSummary.summary: Starting in version 2609, CMG storage shared-key access is disabled. The CMG server application now requires permissions to manage storage role assignments, and Microsoft.Maintenance must be registered for the subscription.
englishSummary.adminImpact: Verify the required service-principal permissions and provider registration for every CMG resource group before updating. Missing permissions can cause deployment updates to fail with HTTP 403 errors.

-Configuration Manager rotates the storage account key for the CMG. This process happens automatically every 180 days.
+For CMG deployments that use shared-key storage access on versions earlier than 2609, Configuration Manager rotates the storage account key automatically every 180 days. @@ -87,7 +86,13 @@ The CMG resources in Azure are part of the Azure platform as a service (PaaS). T
 
 The service principals are authenticated by the server app registration in Microsoft Entra ID. This app is also known as the *web app*. You create this app registration automatically when you create the CMG, or manually by an Azure administrator in advance. For more information, see [Manually register Microsoft Entra apps for the CMG](manually-register-azure-ad-apps).
 
-The secret keys for the Azure apps are encrypted and stored in the Configuration Manager site database. As part of the setup process, the server app has **Read Directory Data** permission to the Microsoft Graph API. It also has the contributor role on the resource group that hosts the CMG. Each time the app needs to access resources like Microsoft Graph, it gets an access token from Azure, which it uses to access the cloud resource.
+The secret keys for the Azure apps are encrypted and stored in the Configuration Manager site database. As part of the setup process, the server app has **Read Directory Data** permission to the Microsoft Graph API. Its service principal also needs **Contributor** or equivalent resource-management permissions on the resource group that hosts the CMG. Each time the app needs to access resources like Microsoft Graph, it gets an access token from Azure, which it uses to access the cloud resource.
+
+For Microsoft Entra-authenticated storage, the server application also needs permission to manage the required **Storage Blob Data Contributor** and **Storage Table Data Contributor** role assignments. Contributor alone doesn't grant permission to create role assignments. Use a **Role Based Access Control Administrator** assignment constrained to those two storage data roles at the CMG resource group, or equivalent approved permissions. Verify inherited access and any conditions before adding a new assignment. For details, see [Configure Azure RBAC permissions for the server app](configure-azure-ad#configure-azure-rbac-permissions-for-the-server-app).
+
+The administrator who grants these permissions needs the appropriate Azure RBAC privileges at the target scope. Registering **Microsoft.Maintenance** separately requires provider-registration permission at the subscription scope. These operator permissions aren't the same as the runtime permissions granted to the CMG application. For details, see [Configure Azure resource providers](configure-azure-ad#configure-azure-resource-providers).
+
+Disabling shared-key access to the storage account doesn't remove the server application's client-secret requirement. Storage account keys and Microsoft Entra application secrets are different credentials.
 
 Microsoft Entra ID can automatically rotate the secret key for these apps, or you can do it manually. When the secret key changes, you need to [renew the secret key](../../../servers/deploy/configure/azure-services-wizard#bkmk_renew) in Configuration Manager.

@@ -123,6 +122,12 @@ Configuration Manager updates Microsoft Visual C++ Redistributable to version 14
 
 Shared key access is automatically disabled for cloud management gateway (CMG) storage, even if you haven't previously selected the option to disable it in the console.
 
+Important
+
+Before updating a site that has a CMG, verify that the CMG server application's service principal has the required Azure role-assignment permissions at the CMG resource group, and that **Microsoft.Maintenance** is registered in the subscription. Existing CMGs that previously used shared-key access also need these prerequisites. Missing permissions or provider registration can cause the CMG deployment update to fail.
+
+For the required permissions and verification steps, see [Configure Azure RBAC permissions for the server app](../../clients/manage/cmg/configure-azure-ad#configure-azure-rbac-permissions-for-the-server-app) and [Configure Azure resource providers](../../clients/manage/cmg/configure-azure-ad#configure-azure-resource-providers).
+
 ### CMG virtual machine scale set image uses Windows Server 2022
 
 Cloud management gateway (CMG) virtual machine scale sets use a supported Windows Server 2022 image offer that doesn't include the deprecated .NET 6 packages. For more information, see [KB 37942646](../../../hotfix/2603/37942646).

englishSummary.headline: New CMG update prerequisites documented
englishSummary.summary: The version 2609 documentation now instructs administrators to verify the CMG server application's Azure role-assignment permissions at the CMG resource group and ensure Microsoft.Maintenance is registered in the subscription before updating a site with a CMG.
englishSummary.adminImpact: Complete these permission and resource-provider checks before updating the site to help avoid update issues.

 description: Learn about actions to take before updating to Configuration Manager version 2609.

@@ -137,6 +136,16 @@ Microsoft ODBC Driver for SQL Server version **18.7.1.1** has a known issue with
 
 For minimum required versions, validated versions, and versions with known blocking issues, see [Prerequisite checks - ODBC driver for SQL Server](../deploy/install/list-of-prerequisite-checks#odbc-driver-for-sql-server).
 
+### Verify Azure prerequisites for existing CMGs
+
+If your hierarchy uses a cloud management gateway (CMG), verify its Azure prerequisites before updating the site. Version 2609 automatically disables shared-key access for CMG storage, including deployments where you haven't previously selected that option.
+
+- Verify that the CMG **server/web application's service principal** has the required resource-management and storage role-assignment permissions at the CMG resource group. Contributor alone doesn't grant permission to create role assignments. Use appropriately constrained permissions as described in [Configure Azure RBAC permissions for the server app](../../clients/manage/cmg/configure-azure-ad#configure-azure-rbac-permissions-for-the-server-app).
+- Verify that **Microsoft.Maintenance** is registered in every subscription containing a CMG, along with the other [required resource providers](../../clients/manage/cmg/configure-azure-ad#configure-azure-resource-providers). Wait until registration is complete.
+- Allow time for permission changes to propagate, then verify the effective access for each CMG server application and resource group. Check production separately from staging: role assignments are scoped to Azure resources, and provider registration is subscription-scoped. Neither change is tenant-wide.
+
+These prerequisites apply to existing deployments even if earlier CMG updates succeeded. Missing permissions or registration can cause the CMG deployment update to fail. For error details, review **CloudMgr.log** and the failed Azure deployment operations.
+
 ### Review the site and hierarchy status for unresolved issues
 
 A site update can fail because of existing operational problems. Before you update a site, resolve all operational issues for the following systems:
@@ -280,6 +289,10 @@ Make sure each site server and site system role is updated to version 2609. In t
 
 Consider restarting remote site systems that don't successfully update at first. Review your site infrastructure and make sure that applicable site servers and remote site system servers successfully restarted. Typically, site servers restart only when Configuration Manager installs .NET as a prerequisite for a site system role.
 
+### Verify CMG deployment and client communication
+
+After updating a site that has a CMG, verify that the CMG deployment update completes successfully. Review **CloudMgr.log** and any failed Azure deployment operations. After the CMG is running, use the [CMG connection analyzer](../../clients/manage/cmg/monitor-clients-cloud-management-gateway#connection-analyzer) to verify communication.
+
 ### Review SQL Server client components
 
 Starting in version 2609, Configuration Manager automatically installs Microsoft OLE DB Driver for SQL Server on site servers and on computers that host the SMS Provider or a management point. SQL Server Native Client is no longer required. For more information, see [Site and site system prerequisites](../../plan-design/configs/site-and-site-system-prerequisites).

englishSummary.headline: Version 2609 adds CMG Azure prerequisite checks
englishSummary.summary: The checklist now states that version 2609 automatically disables shared-key access for CMG storage and adds prerequisites for existing CMGs, including service-principal role-assignment permissions and Microsoft.Maintenance registration.
englishSummary.adminImpact: Before updating, verify permissions and provider registration, allow changes to propagate, and validate CMG deployment and client communication afterward. Missing prerequisites can cause the update to fail.
